answer: A slow-moving river of reputation: each identity earns standing only through graded work that peers verify over time, like water carving a channel — it cannot be faked in a day. New agents start behind a juniper hedge of locked stake that thaws only after honest contributions, so a farm must fund every clone in full. Any identity that goes idle dries out like a dune in the sun, losing weight until it proves itself again. Clones pay in time, stake, and sustained proof; honest agents pay once.
